prospective_cases: CC4-T01
Booking versus travel
Reservations grow, but no comparable completed-service cohort is available.
Report the reservation observation; do not equate it to completed consumption.
CC4-T02
Lead-time ratio
Current revenue is divided by new bookings with a different service-date distribution.
Do not infer a contractual take-rate change without aligned cohorts.
CC4-T03
Cancel and rebook
One trip is canceled and replaced with a new reservation.
Do not count two completed trips; preserve event lineage and time.
CC4-T04
Supplier cash
Deferred merchant cash includes amounts payable to service providers.
Do not classify all cash as earned revenue or surplus shareholder cash.
CC4-T05
Partial cash bridge
CFO less one liability change is calculated.
Label partial bridge, not normalized CFO/FCF/earnings.
CC4-T06
Percent margin
Incremental service revenue exceeds its variable costs while total margin percentage falls.
Preserve contribution gain and margin change; do not silently decide full profitability.
CC4-T07
Shared consumption
A stay appears in owner revenue, brand statistics and platform gross bookings.
Do not sum them into independent consumer expenditure or confirmations.
CC4-T08
Occupancy convention
Cruise occupancy exceeds 100% using double-occupancy capacity.
Preserve denominator; do not clip, flag impossible, or compare directly to hotel occupancy.
CC4-T09
Net yield
A company-defined Net Yield rises while EBITDA per capacity falls.
Retain both with definitions; do not call Net Yield final unit profit.
CC4-T10
Capacity returns
Total contribution grows because capital-intensive capacity expanded.
Require capital and financing analysis before concluding improved returns.
CC4-T11
Hotel conversions
A new branded opening is a conversion of an existing property.
Do not count it automatically as incremental market physical capacity.
CC4-T12
Pipeline
Signed or approved pipeline includes properties not yet operating.
Do not treat pipeline as current fee-producing rooms.
CC4-T13
Guidance basis
Forward fees rise when both RevPAR assumptions and card contracts change.
Distinguish basis changes; management guidance is not consensus or demand-only attribution.
CC4-T14
Owner hurdle
Base fees depend on revenue and incentives have owner-return thresholds.
Do not apply one universal fee sensitivity or infer undisclosed contract rates.
CC4-T15
Reimbursement
Cost reimbursement revenue differs from reimbursed expenses.
Preserve both; do not assume identical pass-through or pure fee revenue.
CC4-T16
Capital period
Quarter EBITDA is compared with first-half renewal spending.
Disallow a quarterly cash-flow label from mismatched periods.
CC4-T17
Comparable population
A later property cohort includes changed acquisition/disposition eligibility.
Preserve the cohort vintage; do not create point-in-time history from current membership.
CC4-T18
App and direct
Mobile app share rises but paid sourcing is unknown.
Do not call app traffic free acquisition or infer cohort profit.
CC4-T19
Corporate action
Retrospectively split-adjusted EPS is combined with an unadjusted historic price.
Require consistent corporate-action bases through the existing identity/market owner.
CC4-T20
Buyer geography
A destination line grows in Japan.
Do not infer Japanese-resident or Japanese-national customer demand.
CC4-T21
Currency signs
Reported growth is negative and constant-currency growth positive.
Explain different bases instead of discarding one as erroneous.
CC4-T22
Workshop capacity
A workshop opens and later facilities are planned.
Do not infer qualified production, utilization, backlog, shortage or unrestricted demand.
CC4-T23
Profit exposure
One business has different shares of revenue and recurring profit.
Keep denominators separate and preserve negative elimination rows.
CC4-T24
Subsidy location
Marketing subsidies are moved to contra revenue.
Count economic support once; no automatic acquisition-efficiency claim or double adjustment.
CC4-T25
Segment vintage
A company provides newly defined segments with recast prior comparisons.
Keep the disclosure vintage; do not assume earlier investors knew the new segmentation.
CC4-T26
Undisclosed geography
Transaction-services revenue is labeled Temu and marketing domestic.
Reject unsupported allocation; retain source categories and unknown geography.
CC4-T27
Historical stress
A 2020 unit-revenue gain accompanied a demand collapse.
Use as a counterexample, not current conditions, ordinary-cycle calibration or shock probability.
CC4-T28
Sampling and access
Survey documentation is read; daily TSA endpoint fails.
Do not claim survey microdata, a live daily feed or global coverage.
CC4-T29
Positive control
Comparable hotel EBITDA and margin improve while maintenance is required.
Preserve the supported improvement and separately disclose capital obligations.
CC4-T30
Missing valuation
No market prices or consensus archive was acquired.
Do not label stocks cheap, expensive, expected winners or investment-validated.
CC4-T31
Source dependence
Several issuers discuss the same macro travel shock.
Cluster shared drivers; do not count each narrative as independent evidence.
CC4-T32
Authority
Research scenarios and source observations are placed in a proposed dossier.
Keep all decision-authority flags false; no basket or trading promotion.
